patch_description:
This design replaces endpoint-regression blending with a causal robust alpha-beta state tracker. It uses the sliding window primarily for local noise estimation and multi-horizon slope agreement, rather than repeatedly fitting complete signal levels.

The tracker predicts the next endpoint from its persistent level and velocity state, then applies a robust, Huber-limited innovation update. A recent slope and a longer slope modulate only the internal alpha/beta gains: agreement increases responsiveness, while disagreement reduces velocity adaptation and prevents short-lived noise bursts from creating false reversals. Reversal confirmation additionally requires persistent opposing slope evidence before weak opposite innovations can overturn an established trend.

This preserves endpoint alignment and API compatibility, while targeting lower reversal counts, reduced noise sensitivity, and low-lag trend tracking.
